contributions.statement: When a new developer's Java change uses syntax or APIs the team has not taught, do not treat the diff as proof they either copied an agent or understood the change; ask what they did after the agent's answer, because a fluent submission can hide either pasting or unlogged study.
contributions.evidence: §4.3 quotes one undergraduate co-author on notes, practice, and re-solving after an AI answer, and §4.2 quotes the same person learning Java syntax by asking a model to explain it. §5.2 says this student is highly motivated and not representative. No second student, no count of either behavior, and no class outcome.

reason: The paper's accuracy claim is three authors reading their own transcripts. The only actionable sentence is a boundary on reading a fluent diff, and it restates, with weaker evidence, the existing caution that a submission is not proof of understanding. It cannot back a gate.
